text:
Overall score: 5/10.

The code is fairly readable and the math is better tested than I expected, but I would not approve it as-is. The main blockers are bootstrap/runtime reliability, missing validation around config/data assumptions, weak story-generation hardening, and important paths that are either untested or only tested on CPU.

I tried `pytest -q`; collection failed because this environment does not have the package/deps installed (`emovec`, `numpy`, etc.), so I could not confirm the suite here.

issues.description: generate-stories requires an existing data/stories/manifest.json, so a fresh checkout cannot bootstrap the dataset.
Providing only hf_model or tokenizer silently discards the supplied object and reloads both from model_name.
from_pretrained uses dtype= instead of the more compatible torch_dtype= argument for the declared transformers dependency range.
last_token_activations leaves indexing tensors on CPU while hidden states may be on CUDA, and this path is not covered by GPU tests.
choice_logits leaves choice_ids, idx, and last on CPU while logits may be on CUDA, making GPU behavior unverified and fragile.
Story-generation HTTP requests have no timeout, retry, or response-status handling, so runs can hang indefinitely or fail opaquely.
Raw emotion names are used as directory names, allowing path traversal or unintended writes if config input is untrusted.
Raw emotion names are interpolated into output filenames, allowing path traversal or invalid filenames from config/manifest data.
Extraction does not validate that every configured emotion has at least one story before computing vectors.
emotion_vectors silently produces NaNs when an emotion label has no examples.
pca_components does not validate zero-variance inputs or variance_target bounds, so degenerate data can produce NaNs.
Validation assumes at least two emotions; a one-emotion config yields empty off-diagonal statistics and NaN summaries.
n_steered_emotions is not bounded or validated, which can duplicate selected emotions or produce empty/misleading steering outputs.
Steering hooks depend on mutable self._steer_mask state, making choice_logits non-reentrant and unsafe for concurrent use.
Default tests exclude the real-model integration path, so the advertised end-to-end pipeline is not exercised by make test.
Hook/model tests only instantiate a CPU tiny model, leaving CUDA device-placement bugs untested.
Generated egg-info and outputs artifacts are present in the workspace despite ignore rules, adding cleanup noise and reproducibility risk.
